findings.reason: the node's positive verdict is its whole product, and a false "receives" is exactly the claim a later section would declare `input_modalities` on clive from, so the plan would be built on a measurement that cannot distinguish a lane that sees from one that sees nothing.
findings.text: the "receives" verdict ("every probe claim matches, the blank control reports no content, and each run opened only its PNG") is satisfied vacuously by a probe that reports "shows none", because the brief explicitly offers that answer and an empty claim set makes "every probe claim matches" trivially true, while "not delivered" is defined to require the Read to have failed — so a lane that receives no image and honestly says so is scored "receives"

findings.reason: a worker hitting this case must either invent a verdict or stop, and the recorded result would not be comparable with the definition the plan states.
findings.text: the three named verdicts do not cover a probe that receives the image but misstates a claim (some bar values match, one wrong): that outcome satisfies neither "every probe claim matches", nor "confabulates" (defined only as the blank control describing content), nor "not delivered" (defined only as a failed Read or a refusal), so the report requirement to "state one verdict" is unsatisfiable for the most likely partial outcome
